Theme

Nature & food

organic adjective

of food and farming: grown without artificial chemicals

also organic food, organic farming, organically grown, organic produce, bio

* our formation

M-O s.v. pesticide: venēnum insectīs internecīvum (Egger)

* (our own formation) sine venēnīs cultus, culta, cultum

phrase: the participle of colō, agreeing with the food

grown without poisons (pesticides)

No reference work has a Latin word for organic food (Morgan–Owens gives only the modern languages’ words). A plain description: venēnum, any strong drug or poison, is the pesticide (Morgan–Owens, after Egger), and cultus is “grown, farmed”.

Other words

  • * (our own formation) biologicus, biologica, biologicum — organic, “bio”

    declension · also used · * our formation · M-O s.v. organic (of food): Fr. biologique, It. biologico; Levi–Bini p. 10, s.v. biologico: ad animantium vītae pertinēns

    The Greek-formed word of the modern languages’ “bio” food; Levi & Bini render “biological” by a phrase, “belonging to the life of living things”, and give the word only for the biologist, biologus. Clear to a European listener, but a label, not a description.

  • organicus, organica, organicum — mechanical; musical

    declension · avoid · classical · Vitr. 10.1.5 (Lewis & Short)

    Classically “of instruments”: mechanical, or musical (Lewis & Short); modern Latin uses it for organic in the sense of living matter (M-O s.v. organic), never of food.

Examples

  • Haec māla sine venēnīs culta sunt.

    These apples are organic.composed

See also natural, chemical.

SourcesLewis & Short: venenum · Lewis & Short: colo · Lewis & Short: organicus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. organic; s.v. pesticide.
